Your next ChatGPT answer might not be text. It might be an app.
On October 7th, OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 with a feature called Intelligent UI.
Ask how a bike works, and you can tap its parts and explore them, instead of reading a paragraph.
Ask to split a dinner bill, and it builds a working bill splitter right inside the chat.
Here's the unseen part. The model isn't drawing pixels. It picks from a library of ready-made components.
Buttons, charts, forms, diagrams. It decides which to use, and how to arrange them.
A compiler turns that plan into a real interface, streaming it onto your screen as the model writes.
OpenAI says it also learned when plain text is enough, so not every answer becomes a widget.
The idea: instead of you learning the software, the software shapes itself around your question.
Latoon. Voyaging the unseen. Follow for more.
